How do you change m/s into km/h?

back: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Instantaneous speed is the speed at one moment (a speedometer reading).
Speed in a particular direction, e.g. 15 m/s north.
$a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{t}$: change in velocity ÷ time taken.

front: What does an acceleration of 3 m/s² mean?
back: The velocity increases by 3 m/s every second.
Slowing down. It gives a negative acceleration, e.g. −5 m/s².
The object is stopped (stationary). Its distance isn't changing.
Constant speed. The steeper the line, the faster. Speed = gradient.
Constant speed (stopped only if the line is at zero).
Speeding up (accelerating). Acceleration = gradient = change in speed ÷ time.

front: Can an object accelerate at a steady speed?
back: Yes, if its direction changes (e.g. going round a roundabout), because its velocity changes.
